findings.title: Partial regex matching corrupts rates and can throw
findings.body: Every string ending in `%` enters this branch, but the unanchored regex extracts only the first digit sequence and assumes one exists. Consequently `-25%` returns `0.25`, `.5%` returns `0.05`, `1e2%` returns `0.01`, malformed `abc25%` is accepted as `0.25`, and `%` throws a TypeError. This can silently apply incorrect rates or crash callers.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `%`, parse the complete remaining token with `Number`, divide by 100, and explicitly return `NaN` for an empty token so malformed input cannot crash or be partially accepted.

next_steps: Replace partial regex extraction with complete-token conversion and verify signed, fractional, exponent, empty, and malformed percentage inputs.
